title: On-Time Delivery
summary: Orders or services delivered by committed date.
whyPeCares: PE cares because this KPI gives an early read on growth quality, margin expansion, cash conversion, execution discipline, or exit-story credibility.
goodBadSignals: Good performance shows controlled execution and improving unit economics; bad performance signals leakage, weak process ownership, or a diligence risk requiring deeper segmentation.
improvementActions: Standardize the definition and data owner.
Segment by customer, site, product, team, or channel.
Tie movement to an operating playbook and weekly cadence.

articleSections.title: The Strategic Impact of OTD on Enterprise Value
body: In the industrial and logistics sectors of private equity, On-Time Delivery (OTD) is not just a customer service metric—it is a critical 'Operating Leverage' and 'Revenue Protection' indicator. We define OTD as the (Number of Orders Delivered On-Time / Total Number of Orders) * 100. A high OTD rate is the primary driver of 'Customer Stickiness' and is often the difference between a 10x and 12x exit multiple, as it de-risks the future revenue stream.

The math of OTD is unforgiving: even a 95% rate means that 1 in 20 customers is experiencing a 'Service Failure'. In a $200M revenue business, that represents $10M in potentially 'At-Risk' revenue. Operating partners look for 'Quality of OTD' by measuring 'On-Time to Promise' (against the original date given to the customer) and 'On-Time to Request' (against the date the customer actually wanted). The gap between these two identifies the 'Operational Constraint' that is limiting growth.

We deploy Transportation Management Systems (TMS) and Warehouse Management Systems (WMS) like Manhattan Associates or Blue Yonder to track every milestone in the 'Order-to-Cash' cycle. By digitizing the 'Logistics Tail,' we can move from manual tracking to a 'Control Tower' model where 'Late Exceptions' are flagged in real-time. This allows management to intervene before the customer is even aware of the delay, preserving the 'Value of the Brand'.
articleSections.callout: OTD is the final validator of your entire supply chain. If your delivery is late, the quality of your product is irrelevant.

articleSections.title: Root Cause Analysis of 'Delivery Gaps'
body: To improve OTD, the operator must look beyond the 'Last Mile' and conduct a 'End-to-End' audit of the supply chain. We use the 'Pareto Principle' to identify the 20% of causes driving 80% of the delays. These typically fall into three buckets: Inventory Shortages, Production Bottlenecks, or Logistics Inefficiency. By isolating these factors, we can apply capital and management focus to the areas with the highest 'Incremental ROI'.

The math of 'Safety Stock' is a primary lever: we use the 'Normal Distribution' of lead times to calculate exactly how much inventory is needed to achieve a 98% service level. If our current OTD is 90% but our inventory turns are 15x, we are likely 'Under-Stocked'. Conversely, if OTD is 99% but inventory is sitting for 6 months, we have 'Trapped Working Capital' that could be better deployed elsewhere. We aim for the 'Golden Mean' where OTD is maximized without bloating the balance sheet.

We implement 'Carrier Scorecards' to hold our logistics partners accountable. By tracking 'Carrier OTD' and 'Damaged Goods' rates, we can drive pricing concessions or consolidate volume into higher-performing carriers. We utilize 'Real-Time Visibility' tools like Project44 or FourKites to track shipments in transit, providing the 'Data Transparency' required to manage customer expectations and reduce the 'Internal Cost of Inquiries'.

articleSections.title: The 'Perfect Order' Metric and Operational Rigor
body: Operating partners often move beyond simple OTD toward the 'Perfect Order' metric. A 'Perfect Order' is one that is delivered: 1) On-Time, 2) In-Full (OIF), 3) Damage-Free, and 4) With Correct Documentation. The math is multiplicative: 95% OTD * 95% OIF * 98% Damage-Free = 88.4% Perfect Order rate. This metric exposes the 'True Level of Operational Friction' that is eroding customer lifetime value.

The operator implements 'Daily Stand-ups' and 'Red/Green Boards' at the shipping dock to maintain a 'High-Cadence' focus on delivery performance. We track 'Dock-to-Door' time as a critical leading indicator. If the warehouse is taking 48 hours to process an order that only takes 24 hours to ship, the 'Internal Inefficiency' is the primary driver of late deliveries. We use 'Lean Manufacturing' principles to eliminate 'Wasteful Motion' and 'Unnecessary Buffer' in the warehouse.

By integrating WMS data with CRM tools like Salesforce, we can calculate the 'LTV of an OTD Customer' vs. a 'Late Customer'. The data invariably shows that late deliveries are the single biggest predictor of 'Customer Churn'. This 'Value Proof' is used to justify investments in 'Automated Picking' or 'Advanced Demand Forecasting' tools that stabilize the OTD rate and improve long-term profitability.

articleSections.title: Scaling OTD Through 'Network Optimization'
body: In a multi-site platform, OTD is often a function of 'Network Design'. We use 'Network Optimization' tools like Llamasoft to determine the 'Optimal Node' for each shipment. By placing inventory closer to the customer, we not only improve OTD but also reduce the 'Outbound Freight Cost'. This 'Double Win' is a primary driver of 'EBITDA Margin Expansion' in industrial distribution platforms.

We track 'Zonal Delivery Performance' to identify geographic 'Dead Zones' where our delivery promise is consistently broken. The operating partner uses this data to decide whether to open a new 'Satellite DC' or to partner with a 'Third-Party Logistics' (3PL) provider. The math is simple: if the 'Cost of Late Delivery' (churn + penalties) exceeds the 'Cost of Extra Node,' we expand the network.

By utilizing 'Predictive Analytics' to anticipate 'Demand Spikes' (e.g., seasonality or promos), we can 'Pre-Position' inventory and ensure that our OTD remains stable even during peak periods. This 'Proactive Capacity Management' is what separates top-quartile operators from those who are constantly in 'Expedite Mode,' which carries a high 'Premium Freight' cost that erodes margins.

articleSections.title: Exit Readiness: Proving the 'Reliability Moat'
body: As we approach the exit, the 'OTD Rate' is presented as a 'Competitive Moat' and a 'Quality Indicator'. We show potential buyers that our high OTD is the result of a 'Digitized, Scalable Process' that is not dependent on individual heroics. We provide 'OTD Trends by Customer Tier,' proving that we are delivering a 'Premium Service' to our most valuable accounts.

We calculate the 'Reliability Premium'—the additional pricing power we command in the market due to our superior delivery performance. Buyers will pay a higher multiple for a business that is 'Mission Critical' to its customers because it never misses a deadline. Proving that the platform can 'Scale Delivery Excellence' is the final 'Value Proof' required for a successful exit.

The final 'Exit Deck' must bridge the 'OTD Gap' from entry to exit, showing how the improvement in delivery contributed to 'Market Share Gains' and 'EBITDA Growth'. By quantifying the millions of dollars in 'Enterprise Value' created through logistics rigor, we justify a 'Multiple Expansion' and deliver the outsized returns our LPs demand.
